response.title: My trolling motor is 36 volt but I only have room for two batteries. Can I run it on 24 volts with lithium, and what do I lose?
response.answer:
Yes, some 36V trolling motors will run on 24V lithium batteries, but many won't—and I wouldn't recommend it without checking your specific motor.

The biggest issue isn't lithium versus lead-acid. It's whether your trolling motor's electronics can operate safely at the lower voltage.

What do you lose going from 36V to 24V?

Assuming your motor can operate at 24V:

Performance

	

36V

	

24V




Maximum thrust

	

100%

	

Potentially significantly less




Top boat speed

	

Full

	

Lower




Performance in wind/current

	

Full

	

Reduced




Motor efficiency

	

Designed operating point

	

May be worse




Spot-Lock / GPS anchoring

	

Normal

	

May struggle or shut down




Risk of low-voltage shutdown

	

Low with healthy batteries

	

Higher

For a simple DC motor, reducing voltage from 36V to 24V could reduce maximum motor speed by roughly one-third under comparable conditions. Actual thrust loss is harder to predict and depends on the motor, propeller, and controller.

Important: A 36V motor isn't necessarily a 24V/36V dual-voltage motor. Some electronic controllers won't even start at 24V.

Real-world example: Garmin Force

The Garmin Force is designed for both voltages, and Garmin publishes these specifications:

36V

100 lb
Maximum thrust

24V

80 lb
Maximum thrust

That's a 20% reduction in maximum thrust, not necessarily a 33% reduction. But these figures apply specifically to the Garmin Force, not all trolling motors. 
Motor Thrust and Current-Draw Information
+1

A better solution for your two-battery space

If your motor requires 36V, consider:

One 36V 100Ah LiFePO4 battery: Full voltage with only one battery.

Two 18V lithium batteries in series: Possible if the manufacturer explicitly supports series operation and the charging arrangement.

Two 12V lithium batteries: Only 24V in series, so not suitable for a 36V-only motor.

For a 36V 100Ah lithium battery, nominal stored energy is approximately 3.84 kWh, giving substantial runtime depending on motor draw. Make sure the battery's BMS, charger, and circuit protection meet the motor manufacturer's specifications.

One question that will determine your best option

What brand and model is your 36V trolling motor? For example, Minn Kota Ultrex 112, Ultrex QUEST, Garmin Force, or Lowrance Ghost.

With that information, I can tell you whether it will actually run on 24V lithium, how much thrust you'll lose, and whether you can keep full 36V performance with just one battery.
